## Historical audit — S0088

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/generic_same_structured_evidence/C1/development/commons_118588033/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 2 is visible; the reference and rendered images themselves are not visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and limits |
|---|---|
| Line 19, student `model_request`, characters [0,194356) | The stated task was to reconstruct an indoor photograph as editable Blender geometry and match viewpoint, framing and materials. The student interpreted it as a ship accommodation compartment; that semantic identification is not independently verified. |
| Line 19, student programs and embedded execution feedback, characters [0,194356) | The programs constructed multiple grouped objects: architecture, bunks, lockers, chair, heater, pipes and lamps. Parts were grouped and positioned with explicit coordinates; the last program added heater mounting rods and rotated the chair about a pivot. These operations do not prove physical contact or correct pose. Color assignments, procedural floor bump and emissive lamp materials were coded, but their appearance and reference fidelity are unknown. |
| Line 19, student revisions, characters [0,194356) | After step 1, the student *diagnosed* low rear objects and lamps, distant lockers and an obstructing right wall; it changed camera position and target, moved lockers and revised the wall while retaining a 27 mm lens. After step 2, it *diagnosed* excessive cropping and a hidden chair, then moved cabinets and heater inward, advanced and rotated the chair, extended the partition and adjusted fill light. These are student assessments, not independent visual findings. |
| Line 19, embedded runner feedback, characters [0,194356); line 17, `execution_result`, characters [0,48417) | Steps 1 and 2 were reported usable; step 3 completed successfully, saved a render and Blender file, and logged 16/16 samples despite the program requesting 64. This validates execution and output creation, not camera, lighting, texture, geometry or visual match. |
| Lines 20–22, `codex_session`, `model_response`, `select` | The final read-only student session had the reference and three renders supplied, no tool calls, and returned `SELECT 3`; the recorded selection is step 3. The session completed normally. |

**Teacher and exploration.** No teacher input, teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or adoption is visible in this chunk. The supplied system and runner instructions guided review; they are not evidence of a teacher intervention. The student performed iterative, render-informed revision within the supplied interaction, but the final session had no autonomous tool exploration (lines 19–20). Earlier unseen evidence cannot be characterized.

**Outcome and lessons.** This is a **technical execution success with visual correctness unknown**, not a demonstrated formal reconstruction success, algorithm failure, empty patch, or interruption. Selection alone is not verification. Transferably, separating a claimed global framing issue from local object edits and retaining a successful lens makes revisions auditable; here, the cropping, occlusion and lighting diagnoses remain task-specific hypotheses. Unresolved are whether the selected render resembles the photograph, whether parts actually connect, whether chair pose and object placements are correct, and whether the procedural surfaces and lighting reproduce the reference.
